text:
sylvia: Seeing AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt when service assumes cross-account role to decrypt S3 envelope key. Started after yesterday's key rotation. Anyone run into a grant/session-policy interaction like this?
raj: Hmm. Is the error from AWS KMS or from the application decrypt call? Any CloudTrail kms:Decrypt entries?
sylvia: CloudTrail shows KMS Deny: "AccessDeniedException" for the assumed-role principal arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/prod-service/AWSCLI-session. The CMK is in account 111111111111. We rotate CMK nightly via automation.
mina: Common culprits: key policy not allowing the cross-account role, or the principal has an IAM session policy that removes kms:Decrypt. Also grants/grant-tokens during rotation can bite.
raj: Can you paste the minimal key policy and the assume-role session policy (sanitized)? Small snippets help.
sylvia: Key policy (redacted):
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowUseOfKey",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
The cross-account role isn't explicitly in the key policy because we relied on IAM policies previously.
mina: That's the issue. If you rely on IAM principal policies for KMS, the key policy must allow that principal or allow IAM principal usage via a statement that sets "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/prod-service"} or a wildcard that trusts the account. Otherwise KMS blocks.
raj: Also check for an explicit Deny in any org SCP or session policy. If you rotated the CMK and recreated a new key ARN, grants that existed for the old CMK won't apply to the new one until re-created.
sylvia: We rotated the key and created an alias pointing to the new CMK; automation attempted to migrate grants but maybe missed.
mina: Quick triage steps: 1) run `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-prod-envelope --region us-west-2` 2) check cloudtrail for kms:Decrypt error event detail 3) use `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --grant-tokens <token>` if your client has a grant token.
raj: If you need a short-term workaround, create a grant that allows Decrypt for the assumed-role ARN:
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-prod-envelope \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/prod-service \
  --operations Decrypt \
  --name temporary-decrypt-grant
```
That will let the role decrypt without changing key policy, but grants are ephemeral and must be managed.
sylvia: Good call. Also noticed the assume-role session policy from the app strips kms:Decrypt — we had a narrow session policy to limit access.
mina: Right. Session policies are evaluated against the effective principal permissions; if the session policy denies or omits the action, KMS will still require the principal to have effective kms:Decrypt allowed by either key policy or grants. Remember: KMS checks key policy first, then IAM principal policies. If key policy explicitly denies, nothing helps.
raj: For full fix, add a key-policy statement like:
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowCrossAccountProdService",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/prod-service"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
and remove brittle session-policy restrictions that drop kms:Decrypt unless you enforce it elsewhere.
audit-bot: Note: Creating a grant will emit a KMS CreateGrant CloudTrail event; ensure automation picks it up for rotation.
sylvia: I created the temporary grant and app decrypts succeeded. Going to patch key policy and update rotation automation to regenerate grants. Thanks.
mina: Also add an audit test that simulates assume-role decrypt after rotation to catch regressions.
raj: +1. If anything flaps again ping me and we can script grant reconciliation in the rotation job. :thumbsup:
